To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Chinese consumers have a high expectation of the fast food restaurants’ CSR performance, and they are willing to support companies that are perceived to be responsible and socially responsive.

Chinese fast-food consumers have high expectations of CSR strategies of fast-food companies; they expect fast-food companies to attach more attention to the well-being and nutrition of consumers, and environmental sustainability; and CSR performance is the most influential factor of consumer loyalty behaviors.
Chinese fast food diner's expectations of CSR performance is different from that of the western counterparts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the CSR practices and their impacts on the consumer behavior of fast food restaurants in China.
the relationship between CSR performance and consumer loyalty.
understanding the CSR expectations of Chinese fast-food diner, and investigating the relationships among CSR performance, consumer satisfaction and loyalty behaviors of the consumers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this research is the first to investigate the relationships between the CSR strategies of the restaurant industry in China, consumer satisfaction and loyalty behavior from the perspective of consumers in China.
this study contributes to the existing body of knowledge by identifying a new set of factors which are important to Chinese consumers’ perceptions of CSR.

the Chinese fast-food diner is more likely to be loyal to the brand when he or she is satisfied with the restaurant’s CSR performance, and that the CSR performance is the most influential factor on the consumers’ loyalty behavior compared to customer satisfaction and perceived quality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the study provides a better understanding of the Chinese diners’ expectations and perception of CSR strategies, and the relationships among the CSR strategies, satisfaction and loyalty behaviors of Chinese diners.
we are trying to find a new way of understanding the social responsibility of the fast food industry, from a consumer perspective.
the Chinese consumers’ expectations and perceptions of CSR in the fast food industry are different from the Western counterparts’.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CSR is not a universal concept and that the same CSR strategy may have different effects depending on the cultural background of the consumer.
Chinese consumers are more concerned about the healthiness of fast food than other CSR issues, and this is the most important driver for their loyalty behaviors.
CSR activities are not only beneficial to the company, but also to the consumers.
